tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	# Step 5 Review: Evaluate Classifier Performance
2	
3	- Reviewer transcript: transcripts/24_2026-11-03_reviewer_step5.md
4	- What was reviewed: the diff from step5-start to commit d337b64 (.harness/diffs/step5_diff.patch), plus src/data.py, src/preprocess.py, src/models.py for context.
5	
6	Checks I ran (read-only, by hand from the diff and source; I did not execute the pipeline):
7	- Recomputed the metrics from the saved confusion counts. For logreg: accuracy (17927+20771)/45000 = 0.8600, precision 20771/(20771+4573) = 0.8196, recall 20771/22500 = 0.9232. All match step5_metrics.csv. tn+fp = tp+fn = 22500, so the pooled test set is balanced and n_test = 45000 is consistent with 2017-2018 (2 x 18,000) + 2019-2021 (3 x 3,000).
8	- Checked that `split_by_year` preserves `df` order and that `_split_arrays` takes `years_test` from the same frame, so the `dup_mask` indexing in `run_step5` is aligned with `X_test`.
9	
10	Verified as correct (no comment needed): metrics are computed only on `X_test` from `prepare_split` (preprocessing fit on training years only); `pos_label=1` with the default `average="binary"` everywhere (no macro); confusion matrix uses `labels=[0, 1]` so the order tn, fp, fn, tp is right; the sensitivity subset is a separate table and does not change the main table; `train_duplicate_mask` hashes raw feature vectors and ignores labels, which matches the PLAN definition.
11	
12	## Comments (reviewer)
13	
14	One row per issue. Number the rows 1, 2, 3, ...
15	
16	| # | Severity | Location | Issue | Suggested fix |
17	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
18	| 1 | Medium | src/main.py `run_step5` (lines ~196-217) | `run_step5` calls `train_all_from_split(split)` and so retrains all three models. When the whole pipeline runs (`--step` omitted), Step 4 has already trained the same models, so every model is fit twice. This costs runtime against the 15-minute budget. The two sets of models are also separate fits, so the Step 4 training report and the Step 5 numbers do not describe the same objects (random_state=42 should make them identical, but nothing checks that). I did not time it, so the size of the cost is unknown. | Have `run_step4` return its models and pass them to `run_step5` (`models` argument, train only when `None`), or load them from `save_models` output. |
19	| 2 | Medium | src/evaluate.py `pooled_table`, `confusion_table`, `evaluate_model` | The "test years only" guard `assert_test_years_only` is called only in `run_step5` and in `per_year_table`. The functions that build the main Step 5 table and the confusion table accept any `X_test`/`y_test`, and nothing checks `len(X_test) == len(y_test)`. Someone calling `pooled_table` with training rows would get a silent, leaky "test" table. Today's call path is safe, so this is defensive, not a live bug. | Give `pooled_table` and `confusion_table` a `years_test` argument and call `assert_test_years_only` inside, or at least check the lengths. (If this changes the PLAN signature, update PLAN.md.) |
20	| 3 | Medium | src/evaluate.py `sensitivity_tables`, results/step5_pooled_no_dup.* | The no-duplicate subset changes the class mix: precision drops from about 0.82 to 0.77 and F1 from 0.87 to 0.84, while 7,743 rows are removed. Because the balance is no longer 50/50, the drop in precision is partly a base-rate effect and not only "the model was relying on duplicates". Neither the code nor the table records how many malware and benign rows were excluded or kept, so a reader cannot separate the two effects. I am inferring this from the numbers; I did not compute the class counts. | Add `n_malware` and `n_benign` (kept) and the excluded counts per class to the sensitivity table, or print the majority-class accuracy for the subset next to it. |
21	| 4 | Low | src/evaluate.py `compute_metrics` (line 87) | `zero_division=0` matches PLAN.md, but it hides a degenerate result. If a model predicted no malware, precision would be reported as 0.0 with no warning, which looks like a real score. This does not occur in the current results (the confusion table shows tp > 0 for all models), and it matters most for small slices such as the per-year Step 6 tables. | Keep the setting (it follows PLAN), but add a column or a printed note when `tp + fp == 0` or `tp + fn == 0`, so a 0.0 from zero division is distinguishable from a true 0.0. |
22	| 5 | Low | src/evaluate.py `sensitivity_tables` (line 158) | If every test row is a duplicate (`keep` all False), `model.predict` on an empty array raises a sklearn error with an unclear message. There is also no check that `dup_mask` came from the same test years as `years_test`; `run_step5` relies on the unstated assumption that `df["year"].isin(TEST_YEARS)` selects exactly the rows in `split`. That holds now, but a split built with different test years would misalign the mask silently when lengths happen to match. | Raise a clear `ValueError` when `keep.sum() == 0`. Optionally have `run_step5` assert `len(dup_mask) == len(y_test)` before the call (the function already checks this, so only the comment/assumption needs to be explicit). |
23	| 6 | Low | src/main.py `run_step5` / src/evaluate.py `baseline_accuracy` | The majority-class baseline is printed but not saved to results/. The saved metrics table has no reference for accuracy, and the pooled set is exactly balanced (baseline 0.5), so the 0.86 accuracy cannot be read in context from the CSV alone. | Add a `baseline_accuracy` column or a one-row file in results/. |
24	| 7 | Low | src/evaluate.py, PLAN.md Step 5 | PLAN lists `run_evaluation(df)` as the entry point and says it also writes the Step 6 files and optional figure; the builder put the entry point in `main.run_step5` instead. PLAN also says pooled metrics weight years by size and the per-year table is the primary view; Step 5 output does not carry any note of this (the 2017-2018 rows are 80% of the pooled set). This may be an intentional step-by-step split, so I mark it Low. | Either add `run_evaluation` as planned or update PLAN.md to say the entry point is `run_step5`. Add a one-line note about the 80% weighting to the markdown output or the Step 5 doc. |
25	| 8 | Low (style) | src/main.py `main` | `df = run_step1()` is now unconditional, whereas before it was guarded by `args.step in (None, 1, 2, 3, 4)`. The old guard was always true for allowed steps, so this is a harmless simplification, but `split = None` followed by separate step branches is getting hard to follow as steps are added. Style preference only. | No action required; consider a small dict of step functions when Step 6 is added. |
26	
27	## Decision log (student)
28	
29	One row per comment above, with the same number. Decision is Accepted or Rejected. For accepted comments, add the commit that fixed it.
30	
31	| # | Decision | Reason | Fixed in commit |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| 1 | Accepted | Retraining the same models in Step 5 wastes runtime and means Step 4 and Step 5 describe different objects. Let run_step5 take the models from run_step4 and train only when none are passed, so --step 5 alone still works. | |
34	| 2 | Accepted | Partly: add a check that X_test and y_test have equal length in pooled_table and confusion_table. Do not change the function signatures, because the tester writes tests against the signatures in PLAN.md. | |
35	| 3 | Accepted | The no-duplicate subset changes the class mix, so the precision drop is partly a base-rate effect. Add kept and excluded counts per class (malware and benign) to the sensitivity table and state the majority-class accuracy of the subset in the Step 5 report. | |
36	| 4 | Rejected | The reviewer confirms the situation does not occur: tp is above 0 for all models, and zero_division=0 follows PLAN.md. The per-year slices in Step 6 have 3,000 to 18,000 rows. An extra flag column adds clutter to every results table for a case that is not present. | — |
37	| 5 | Accepted | A clear message beats an unclear sklearn error. Raise ValueError when keep.sum() is 0. The explicit length assert in run_step5 is optional and can be skipped. | |
38	| 6 | Accepted | The 0.86 accuracy cannot be read in context from the CSV alone. Add a baseline_accuracy column to results/step5_metrics.csv (it is 0.5 on the balanced test set). | |
39	| 7 | Accepted | The entry point is main.run_step5, consistent with Steps 1 to 4, so update PLAN.md to say so, in its own commit with the reason. Also add a one-line note to docs/step5_evaluation.md that 2017 and 2018 make up 80 percent of the pooled test set. | |
40	| 8 | Rejected | Style preference on main.py structure, already declined in Steps 1 to 4. Refactoring the step dispatch now adds churn without changing any result. | — |

"""Entry point: python -m src.main [--step N]."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys

import pandas as pd

from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS, TRAIN_YEARS
from src.evaluate import (
    assert_test_years_only,
    baseline_accuracy,
    confusion_table,
    pooled_table,
    save_table,
    sensitivity_tables,
)
from src.models import save_models, train_all_from_split, train_with_report
from src.preprocess import filter_report, prepare_split, split_table
from src.drift import run_drift_analysis
from src.data import (
    _row_hashes,
    train_duplicate_mask,
    feature_columns,
    file_table,
    label_conflict_mask,
    load_all,
    summarize_data,
    write_data_summary,
)


def run_step1() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Step 1: load and combine the data, write results/step1_*.csv|md, print a summary."""
    df = load_all()
    summary = summarize_data(df)
    write_data_summary(summary, RESULTS_DIR / "step1_data_summary")
    write_data_summary(file_table(df), RESULTS_DIR / "step1_file_table")
    n_features = len(feature_columns(df))
    print(f"Step 1: {len(df)} rows, {n_features} feature columns, memory {df.memory_usage().sum() / 1e6:.0f} MB")
    print(summary.to_string(index=False))
    # Feature vectors that occur with both labels anywhere in the data (all years pooled).
    hashes = _row_hashes(df)
    conflict = label_conflict_mask(hashes, df["label"].to_numpy())
    print(f"Label conflicts (all years pooled): {len(set(hashes[conflict]))} vectors, {int(conflict.sum())} rows")
    return df


def run_step2(df: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 2: KS feature drift and the concept-drift accuracy matrix; writes results/step2_*."""
    tables = run_drift_analysis(load_all() if df is None else df)
    for name in ("ks_vs_2014", "ks_consecutive", "accuracy_matrix"):
        print(f"Step 2 {name}:")
        print(tables[name].round(4).to_string())
    return tables


def run_step3(df: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """Step 3: preprocess (fit on 2014-2016 only); writes results/step3_*."""
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS)
    pre = split["preprocessor"]
    counts = filter_report(df, pre, TEST_YEARS)
    table = split_table(split)
    write_data_summary(counts, RESULTS_DIR / "step3_feature_counts")
    write_data_summary(table, RESULTS_DIR / "step3_split")
    write_data_summary(split["clip_stats"], RESULTS_DIR / "step3_clip")
    pd.Series(pre.kept_features_, name="feature").to_csv(RESULTS_DIR / "step3_kept_features.csv", index=False)
    print(f"Step 3: X_train {split['X_train'].shape} {split['X_train'].dtype}, X_test {split['X_test'].shape}")
    print(split["clip_stats"].to_string(index=False))
    print(counts.to_string(index=False))
    print(table.to_string(index=False))
    return split


def run_step4(split: dict | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Step 4: train the three classifiers on 2014-2016; prints TRAINING-only sanity numbers."""
    split = prepare_split(load_all(), TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    models, report = train_with_report(split)
    save_models(models)
    write_data_summary(report, RESULTS_DIR / "step4_training")
    print("Step 4 (training-set sanity check only, NOT evaluation):")
    print(report.to_string(index=False))
    return report


def run_step5(df: pd.DataFrame | None = None, split: dict | None = None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 5: evaluate the three classifiers on the pooled test years 2017-2021; writes results/step5_*."""
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    models = train_all_from_split(split)  # fit on 2014-2016 only
    X_test, y_test, years_test = split["X_test"], split["y_test"], split["years_test"]
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    main_table = pooled_table(models, X_test, y_test)
    # Mask over all rows of df; select the test rows (split_by_year keeps df order).
    dup_mask = train_duplicate_mask(df)[df["year"].isin(TEST_YEARS).to_numpy()]
    no_dup, _ = sensitivity_tables(models, X_test, y_test, years_test, dup_mask)
    confusion = confusion_table(models, X_test, y_test)
    save_table(main_table, "step5_metrics")
    save_table(no_dup, "step5_pooled_no_dup")
    save_table(confusion, "step5_confusion")
    base = baseline_accuracy(y_test)
    print(f"Step 5 (pooled test years, n={len(y_test)}; majority-class accuracy {base:.4f}):")
    print(main_table.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(f"Sensitivity (no exact training duplicate; {int(dup_mask.sum())} test rows excluded):")
    print(no_dup.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(confusion.to_string(index=False))
    return {"metrics": main_table, "no_dup": no_dup, "confusion": confusion}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the pipeline (Steps 1-5 exist so far); --step N runs one step."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Project 2 pipeline")
    parser.add_argument("--step", type=int, choices=range(1, 8), help="run a single step (1-7)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.step not in (None, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5):
        print(f"Step {args.step} is not implemented yet.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1  # non-zero so callers can tell nothing ran
    df = run_step1()
    if args.step in (None, 2):
        run_step2(df)
    split = None
    if args.step in (None, 3):
        split = run_step3(df)
    if args.step in (None, 4):
        run_step4(split)
    if args.step in (None, 5):
        run_step5(df, split)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""Steps 5 and 6: evaluate the trained classifiers on the held-out test years (malware = positive class)."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from typing import Any
5	
6	import numpy as np
7	import pandas as pd
8	from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, confusion_matrix, f1_score, precision_score, recall_score
9	
10	from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS
11	from src.data import write_data_summary
12	
13	METRIC_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = ("accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1")
14	
15	
16	def compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
17	    """Accuracy, precision, recall and F1 with malware (label 1) as the positive class."""
18	    kwargs = {"pos_label": 1, "zero_division": 0}  # zero_division=0: no predicted/actual malware gives 0, not an error
19	    return {
20	        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
21	        "precision": float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
22	        "recall": float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
23	        "f1": float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
24	    }
25	
26	
27	def confusion_counts(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, int]:
28	    """Confusion matrix as TN, FP, FN, TP counts (labels fixed to [0, 1] so a missing class still gives 2x2)."""
29	    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
30	    return {"tn": int(tn), "fp": int(fp), "fn": int(fn), "tp": int(tp)}
31	
32	
33	def assert_test_years_only(years: np.ndarray) -> None:
34	    """Raise ValueError if any year is outside TEST_YEARS (metrics must never be computed on training years)."""
35	    bad = sorted(set(np.unique(years).tolist()) - set(TEST_YEARS))
36	    if bad:
37	        raise ValueError(f"evaluation data contains years outside {TEST_YEARS}: {bad}")
38	
39	
40	def evaluate_model(model: Any, X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
41	    """Predict with a fitted model and return its four metrics."""
42	    return compute_metrics(y_test, model.predict(X_test))
43	
44	
45	def pooled_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
46	    """One row per classifier: model, accuracy, precision, recall, f1, n_test (pooled over the test years)."""
47	    rows = [{"model": name, **evaluate_model(m, X_test, y_test), "n_test": len(y_test)} for name, m in models.items()]
48	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", *METRIC_NAMES, "n_test"])
49	
50	
51	def per_year_table(
52	    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray
53	) -> pd.DataFrame:
54	    """One row per (model, test year): metrics plus year and n."""
55	    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
56	    rows = []
57	    for name, m in models.items():
58	        pred = m.predict(X_test)  # predict once, slice per year
59	        for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
60	            sel = years_test == year
61	            rows.append({"model": name, "year": int(year), **compute_metrics(y_test[sel], pred[sel]), "n": int(sel.sum())})
62	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "year", *METRIC_NAMES, "n"])
63	
64	
65	def confusion_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
66	    """One row per classifier with pooled tn, fp, fn, tp counts."""
67	    return pd.DataFrame([{"model": n, **confusion_counts(y_test, m.predict(X_test))} for n, m in models.items()])
68	
69	
70	def baseline_accuracy(y_test: np.ndarray) -> float:
71	    """Accuracy of always predicting the majority class of y_test."""
72	    return float(max(np.mean(y_test == 1), np.mean(y_test == 0)))
73	
74	
75	def sensitivity_tables(
76	    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray, dup_mask: np.ndarray
77	) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
78	    """Pooled and per-year tables on test rows with NO exact duplicate in the training years (dup_mask False).
79	
80	    Each table gets an n_excluded column (rows removed by the filter; per year for the per-year table).
81	    """
82	    dup_mask = np.asarray(dup_mask, dtype=bool)
83	    if len(dup_mask) != len(y_test):
84	        raise ValueError(f"dup_mask has {len(dup_mask)} entries but there are {len(y_test)} test rows")
85	    keep = ~dup_mask
86	    pooled = pooled_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep])
87	    pooled["n_excluded"] = int(dup_mask.sum())
88	    per_year = per_year_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep], years_test[keep])
89	    excluded = pd.Series(years_test[dup_mask]).value_counts()

# Step 5 Report: Evaluation

Written by the builder agent. All numbers below were produced by `python -m src.main --step 5` (about 23 s including the three model fits) and are saved in `results/`.

## What was done

- `src/evaluate.py` holds the metric code: `compute_metrics` (accuracy, precision, recall, F1 with `pos_label=1`, `zero_division=0`), `confusion_counts`, `evaluate_model`, `pooled_table`, `assert_test_years_only`, `sensitivity_tables`, `save_table`. (`per_year_table` is also there because `sensitivity_tables` returns the per-year table too; it is Step 6 and not reported here.)
- The three Step 4 classifiers (fit on 2014-2016 only, via `train_all_from_split`) are evaluated on the **pooled held-out test years 2017-2021 only**: 45,000 rows (22,500 malware, 22,500 goodware). `assert_test_years_only` raises if any other year is passed. No metric is computed on training rows.
- Malware (label 1) is the positive class.
- Because pooled metrics weight 2017-2018 (18,000 rows each) six times more than 2019-2021 (3,000 each), the pooled numbers are dominated by the early test years. The per-year view is Step 6.

## Main table (all 45,000 test rows)

Files: `results/step5_metrics.csv|md`.

| Classifier | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | n_test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| logreg | 0.8600 | 0.8196 | 0.9232 | 0.8683 | 45000 |
| random_forest | 0.8658 | 0.8228 | 0.9324 | 0.8742 | 45000 |
| sgd | 0.8358 | 0.8063 | 0.8841 | 0.8434 | 45000 |

## Sensitivity: test rows with no exact training duplicate

Files: `results/step5_pooled_no_dup.csv|md`. Test rows whose exact feature vector also occurs in 2014-2016 (`train_duplicate_mask`, Step 1) are removed. This **removes 7,743 of 45,000 test rows (17.2%)**, leaving 37,257. The main table above keeps all rows.

| Classifier | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | n_test | n_excluded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| logreg | 0.8480 | 0.7695 | 0.9318 | 0.8429 | 37257 | 7743 |
| random_forest | 0.8544 | 0.7735 | 0.9434 | 0.8501 | 37257 | 7743 |
| sgd | 0.8475 | 0.7636 | 0.9433 | 0.8440 | 37257 | 7743 |

Accuracy and F1 drop by about 0.5-1.4 points for logreg and random forest (accuracy 0.8600 to 0.8480, 0.8658 to 0.8544), so the duplicates help a little but do not explain the result. SGD changes the least in accuracy (0.8358 to 0.8475, slightly higher). Precision falls in all three (about 0.04-0.05) and recall rises. The removed rows are not a random sample (they are mostly 2017 rows, see Step 1: 5,972 of 18,000), so the filtered set has a different class mix and year mix; I did not break this down further.

## Confusion matrices (pooled, all 45,000 test rows)

Files: `results/step5_confusion.csv|md`. Rows are the true class, columns the predicted class; malware = positive.

| Classifier | TN (goodware ok) | FP (goodware flagged) | FN (malware missed) | TP (malware caught) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| logreg | 17927 | 4573 | 1729 | 20771 |
| random_forest | 17983 | 4517 | 1521 | 20979 |
| sgd | 17721 | 4779 | 2608 | 19892 |

## Baseline

The test set is exactly balanced (50% malware), so always predicting one class gives accuracy 0.5000; logreg (0.8600), random forest (0.8658) and SGD (0.8358) beat that by 33.6-36.6 points, so all three learn real signal even on drifted years.

## Which metric matters most

Recall on malware matters most here: a missed malware app (false negative) is installed and can do harm, while a false alarm on goodware costs a review or a blocked install. Recall is 0.9232 (logreg), 0.9324 (random forest) and 0.8841 (SGD), i.e. 1,729, 1,521 and 2,608 of 22,500 malware apps are missed. Precision is lower (0.81-0.82): about one flagged app in five is goodware. Since the classes are balanced, accuracy is not misleading, but it hides this asymmetry; F1 balances precision and recall but treats both errors alike. All of these pooled numbers are dominated by 2017-2018 and may hide a decline in later years; Step 6 reports it per year.

## Caveats

- The classifiers were trained once with the default settings from Step 4 (no tuning), so differences of about one point between logreg and random forest are small and come from a single fit with `random_state=42`; I did not measure the run-to-run spread.
- Duplicate rows and 107 feature vectors with conflicting labels (Step 1) are kept in the main table, as planned.
- `PLAN.md` names the pooled file `results/step5_pooled_metrics.*`; I used `results/step5_metrics.*` as the lead engineer asked.

2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from typing import Any
5	
6	import numpy as np
7	import pandas as pd
8	from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, confusion_matrix, f1_score, precision_score, recall_score
9	
10	from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS
11	from src.data import write_data_summary
12	
13	METRIC_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = ("accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1")
14	
15	
16	def compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
17	    """Accuracy, precision, recall and F1 with malware (label 1) as the positive class."""
18	    kwargs = {"pos_label": 1, "zero_division": 0}  # zero_division=0: no predicted/actual malware gives 0, not an error
19	    return {
20	        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
21	        "precision": float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
22	        "recall": float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
23	        "f1": float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
24	    }
25	
26	
27	def confusion_counts(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, int]:
28	    """Confusion matrix as TN, FP, FN, TP counts (labels fixed to [0, 1] so a missing class still gives 2x2)."""
29	    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
30	    return {"tn": int(tn), "fp": int(fp), "fn": int(fn), "tp": int(tp)}
31	
32	
33	def assert_test_years_only(years: np.ndarray) -> None:
34	    """Raise ValueError if any year is outside TEST_YEARS (metrics must never be computed on training years)."""
35	    bad = sorted(set(np.unique(years).tolist()) - set(TEST_YEARS))
36	    if bad:
37	        raise ValueError(f"evaluation data contains years outside {TEST_YEARS}: {bad}")
38	
39	
40	def evaluate_model(model: Any, X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
41	    """Predict with a fitted model and return its four metrics."""
42	    return compute_metrics(y_test, model.predict(X_test))
43	
44	
45	def pooled_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
46	    """One row per classifier: model, accuracy, precision, recall, f1, n_test (pooled over the test years)."""
47	    rows = [{"model": name, **evaluate_model(m, X_test, y_test), "n_test": len(y_test)} for name, m in models.items()]
48	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", *METRIC_NAMES, "n_test"])
49	
50	
51	def per_year_table(
52	    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray
53	) -> pd.DataFrame:
54	    """One row per (model, test year): metrics plus year and n."""
55	    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
56	    rows = []
57	    for name, m in models.items():
58	        pred = m.predict(X_test)  # predict once, slice per year
59	        for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
60	            sel = years_test == year
61	            rows.append({"model": name, "year": int(year), **compute_metrics(y_test[sel], pred[sel]), "n": int(sel.sum())})
62	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "year", *METRIC_NAMES, "n"])

64	
65	def confusion_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
66	    """One row per classifier with pooled tn, fp, fn, tp counts."""
67	    return pd.DataFrame([{"model": n, **confusion_counts(y_test, m.predict(X_test))} for n, m in models.items()])

70	def baseline_accuracy(y_test: np.ndarray) -> float:
71	    """Accuracy of always predicting the majority class of y_test."""
72	    return float(max(np.mean(y_test == 1), np.mean(y_test == 0)))

75	def sensitivity_tables(
76	    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray, dup_mask: np.ndarray
77	) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
78	    """Pooled and per-year tables on test rows with NO exact duplicate in the training years (dup_mask False).
79	
80	    Each table gets an n_excluded column (rows removed by the filter; per year for the per-year table).
81	    """
82	    dup_mask = np.asarray(dup_mask, dtype=bool)
83	    if len(dup_mask) != len(y_test):
84	        raise ValueError(f"dup_mask has {len(dup_mask)} entries but there are {len(y_test)} test rows")
85	    keep = ~dup_mask
86	    pooled = pooled_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep])
87	    pooled["n_excluded"] = int(dup_mask.sum())
88	    per_year = per_year_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep], years_test[keep])
89	    excluded = pd.Series(years_test[dup_mask]).value_counts()
90	    per_year["n_excluded"] = per_year["year"].map(lambda y: int(excluded.get(y, 0)))
91	    return pooled, per_year

32	Accuracy and F1 drop by about 0.5-1.4 points for logreg and random forest (accuracy 0.8600 to 0.8480, 0.8658 to 0.8544), so the duplicates help a little but do not explain the result. SGD changes the least in accuracy (0.8358 to 0.8475, slightly higher). Precision falls in all three (about 0.04-0.05) and recall rises. The removed rows are not a random sample (they are mostly 2017 rows, see Step 1: 5,972 of 18,000), so the filtered set has a different class mix and year mix; I did not break this down further.
33	
34	## Confusion matrices (pooled, all 45,000 test rows)
35	
36	Files: `results/step5_confusion.csv|md`. Rows are the true class, columns the predicted class; malware = positive.
37	
38	| Classifier | TN (goodware ok) | FP (goodware flagged) | FN (malware missed) | TP (malware caught) |
39	|---|---|---|---|---|
40	| logreg | 17927 | 4573 | 1729 | 20771 |
41	| random_forest | 17983 | 4517 | 1521 | 20979 |
42	| sgd | 17721 | 4779 | 2608 | 19892 |
43	
44	## Baseline
45	
46	The test set is exactly balanced (50% malware), so always predicting one class gives accuracy 0.5000; logreg (0.8600), random forest (0.8658) and SGD (0.8358) beat that by 33.6-36.6 points, so all three learn real signal even on drifted years.
47	
48	## Which metric matters most
49	
50	Recall on malware matters most here: a missed malware app (false negative) is installed and can do harm, while a false alarm on goodware costs a review or a blocked install. Recall is 0.9232 (logreg), 0.9324 (random forest) and 0.8841 (SGD), i.e. 1,729, 1,521 and 2,608 of 22,500 malware apps are missed. Precision is lower (0.81-0.82): about one flagged app in five is goodware. Since the classes are balanced, accuracy is not misleading, but it hides this asymmetry; F1 balances precision and recall but treats both errors alike. All of these pooled numbers are dominated by 2017-2018 and may hide a decline in later years; Step 6 reports it per year.
51	
52	## Caveats
53	
54	- The classifiers were trained once with the default settings from Step 4 (no tuning), so differences of about one point between logreg and random forest are small and come from a single fit with `random_state=42`; I did not measure the run-to-run spread.
55	- Duplicate rows and 107 feature vectors with conflicting labels (Step 1) are kept in the main table, as planned.
56	- `PLAN.md` names the pooled file `results/step5_pooled_metrics.*`; I used `results/step5_metrics.*` as the lead engineer asked.

content.text:
All six accepted comments are fixed, and `python harness.py test all` passes (182 tests). I reran `python -m src.main --step 5` and regenerated `results/step5_*`. No existing test failed from these changes. Comments 4 and 8 were Rejected, so I left them alone. I did not touch `tests/`, `reviews/` or `transcripts/`.

| Comment | What changed | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `run_step4` now returns `(models, report)`. `run_step5` takes a `models` argument and trains only when it is `None`, so `--step 5` alone still works. | a07b5a0 |
| 2 | Added a length check for `X_test` and `y_test` in `pooled_table` and `confusion_table`, raising `ValueError`. Signatures are unchanged. | 08f6bde |
| 3 | The pooled no-duplicate table now has `n_malware`, `n_benign`, `n_excluded_malware` and `n_excluded_benign`. The run prints the subset's majority-class accuracy. | a0d7d4b |
| 5 | `sensitivity_tables` raises a clear `ValueError` when no test rows are left after the filter. I skipped the optional assert in `run_step5`. | 3833208 |
| 6 | Added a `baseline_accuracy` column to `step5_metrics`. It is 0.5. | 662f07f |
| 7 | `PLAN.md` now says the Step 5 entry point is `main.run_step5`, with the reason, in its own commit. | cda78de |
| 3, 6 | Regenerated `results/step5_*` with the new columns. | b5e4b46 |
| 3, 6, 7 | Updated `docs/step5_evaluation.md`: new tables, the baseline, the 80% weighting note and the class-mix analysis. | f8fa548 |

- **Class mix:** the duplicate filter removes 6,200 malware rows but only 1,543 goodware rows. The subset is 43.8% malware, and always predicting goodware scores 0.5625 on it. So the precision drop from about 0.82 to about 0.77 is partly a base-rate effect, as the reviewer suspected. The report says this.
- **Report corrections:** I also fixed two figures in the report's sensitivity text. The old "0.5–1.4 points" accuracy drop is now 1.1–1.2 points, and F1 drops 2.4–2.5 points.
- **Return type change:** `run_step4` now returns a tuple instead of a DataFrame. No test calls it, and `main` is its only caller.
- **Unfinished:** nothing.
